title: Quantifying the Quarantine
tagline: Simulating a zombie outbreak across a real population map.
summary: A zombie outbreak spreading across Czechia, simulated on a 1 km population map. Every square kilometre runs Munz et al.'s humans–zombies–removed model, with zombies wandering, humans fleeing and the dead rising, as a front of bites sweeps out from Prague, Brno or Ostrava. Draw cordons and seal regions to contain it, built by a single crew at a fixed pace.
about:
**What you're seeing.** Each pixel is one square kilometre of Czechia. Amber light shows where people live. The bright red front is where zombies are biting now, and dark red is land the zombies hold. As people are lost, the lights go out. Point at the map to read a square kilometre.

**The quarantine.** Nobody notices the outbreak until day 7, so until then the map shows nothing amiss. Turn on *Draw cordon* and draw on the map to plan a cordon, or click a region (or choose it under *Seal a region*) to close its borders with the rest of Czechia. One crew builds everything in the order you planned it, at 40 km a day, starting on the day the outbreak is detected. Nothing crosses a finished cordon, but zombies can still leave across the national border. Reset, or a new city or strain, clears the map.

**The model** is the humans–zombies–removed model of Munz et al. (2009), ["When zombies attack!"](https://loe.org/images/content/091023/Zombie%20Publication.pdf), run in every square kilometre:

- zombies bite humans, who become zombies (β); humans destroy zombies (α); and the destroyed rise again (ζ)
- zombies wander into neighbouring squares (D), and humans flee from squares where zombies are a larger share (χ)
- in a square with fewer than one zombie, zombies cannot bite, so a thin scattering of them cannot start an outbreak on its own
- zombies that cross the border are counted, and leave the model; humans stay in Czechia.

**The strains**, the detection day and the crew's speed are illustrative settings, not estimates. *Munz et al. (2009)* uses the paper's rates, reading its population of 500 as 500 people per km². *Shamblers* are slow, *Frenzied* are fast, and *Risers* lose most fights but rise again within days. Change any rate under *Advanced*.

**Still to come:** how many people a quarantine saves, compared with doing nothing.

**Data.** Population: [WorldPop](https://dx.doi.org/10.5258/SOTON/WP00675), Czech Republic 2020, UN-adjusted, regridded to an equal-area 1 km grid ([CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)). Boundaries: [Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/) (public domain).
